title: The Queen's College, Oxford, advertises a career development fellowship in Sanskrit
dek: The John P. Clay fellowship is a three-year post for an early-career Sanskritist, based at the Centre for Manuscript and Text Cultures and starting on 1 September 2027. Applications close on 8 February 2027.
body: The Queen's College, Oxford, is recruiting a John P. Clay Career Development Fellow in Sanskrit. The full-time post is fixed-term for three years from 1 September 2027 and can be renewed for two further years, subject to donor funding. The fellow will be based at the college's Centre for Manuscript and Text Cultures. The vacancy was shared on the INDOLOGY mailing list on 15 November.

The fellow is expected to carry out original research on Sanskrit manuscript and text cultures and to sit on the centre's management committee. The duties include work for the centre's journal and monograph series, finding Sanskrit scholars to write for them, and building links with research institutes in South Asia. The college also mentions optional lecturing at the centre's partner universities in China, Nanjing and Tsinghua.

Teaching averages six weighted hours a week in term time for the university's Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies. The fellow also takes part in undergraduate admissions and, from the second year, gives pastoral support to students. The salary is £43,690 a year plus a discretionary Queen's Weighting of £3,335, with a research allowance of £4,165 a year and meals in the college's Senior Common Room.

Candidates need a doctorate in Sanskrit or a closely related field, conferred or officially confirmed by 1 June 2027, and broad expertise in Sanskrit. The further particulars say they must not have more than two years of full-time research after the doctorate by 1 September 2027; the two years need not be continuous.

Applications are made online, through the college's vacancies page and Interfolio, by 11.59 pm on Monday 8 February 2027, a time the college gives as EST. They need a CV, a covering letter on meeting the teaching requirement, a statement of about 1,500 words on planned research and two confidential references. Shortlisted candidates will be asked for a writing sample of up to 8,000 words, and in-person interviews are expected on 16 March 2027.
